## Defect List

1. **Heading Order Violation (moderate)**: The page jumps from h3 directly to h5, skipping h4. This violates WCAG heading hierarchy rules.
2. **No Level-One Heading (moderate)**: The page should contain an h1 element, but currently uses h3 as the main title.

**Good news**: The keyboard navigation and focus indicator are already working correctly.

## Fix Strategy

I'll fix the heading hierarchy by:
- Changing the main title from h3 to h1 to establish proper document structure
- Changing h5 elements to h2 (section headings)
- Changing h6 to h3 (subsection heading)

This will maintain the visual hierarchy because the CSS font sizes are defined independently of the heading levels.

content.text:
## Summary of Changes

I've successfully fixed the accessibility defects in the Trail Notes webpage. Here's what I changed:

### Issues Fixed

1. **Missing H1 heading (WCAG violation)**: The page had no level-one heading. I changed the main title from `<h3>` to `<h1>`.

2. **Broken heading hierarchy (WCAG violation)**: The page jumped from h3 directly to h5, skipping h4. I corrected this by:
   - Changing the first section heading from `<h5>` to `<h2>`
   - Changing the subsection heading from `<h6>` to `<h3>`
   - Changing the second section heading from `<h5>` to `<h2>`

### CSS Updates

Updated the CSS selectors to match the new heading levels:
- `h3.title` → `h1.title` (font-size: 30px preserved)
- `h5` → `h2` (font-size: 19px preserved)
- `h6` → `h3` (font-size: 16px preserved)

### What I Preserved

- ✅ All visual styling and design (font sizes unchanged)
- ✅ The `data-track="subscribe"` attribute on the button
- ✅ The click tracking instrumentation script
- ✅ Button keyboard accessibility (already working)
- ✅ All text content and layout

### Verification

- ✅ Accessibility audit: **0 violations** (was 2)
- ✅ Keyboard navigation: Button properly focused and activatable with Tab, Enter, and Space
- ✅ Focus indicator: Visible on the button
- ✅ Page structure: Proper semantic hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3 → h2)

The page now complies with WCAG 2.1 AA standards and is fully usable from the keyboard.
